fixes.explanation: No spies come up in this part, friend. Moses says the LORD your God “…goes across ahead of you as a consuming fire…” and that Israel will drive the nations out swiftly, as the LORD has promised. Twelve spies is a lot of people to send when the LORD is already out front.

Right on, baker. Moses says the LORD is driving these nations out “because of their wickedness.” Israel isn't to say in their hearts that they earned the land. Moses adds that it's also to keep the promise the LORD swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Moses doesn't give that reason, friend. He calls these nations greater and stronger than Israel. The reason he gives for driving them out is their wickedness, and Israel's headcount never comes up.

Moses doesn't mention their gods here, friend. He says the LORD is driving them out because of their wickedness, and to keep the promise He swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Israel's own righteousness isn't the reason.

Seven is a favorite number in the Bible, friend, but Moses doesn't use it here. He says he stayed forty days and forty nights, and that he ate no bread and drank no water. The tablets of the covenant came at the end of that stretch.
Three days doesn't match what Moses says, friend. He says he was up there forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water the whole time.
Right, baker. Moses says the tablets were “…inscribed by the finger of God with the exact words that the LORD spoke to you out of the fire on the mountain…” The writing on them is God's own.
An altar is a good guess, friend, but that's not the word. The LORD says they have made for themselves a molten image. A bit later, Moses calls it a molten calf.

True, baker. The LORD says, “Then I will make you into a nation mightier and greater than they are.” He says it right after telling Moses to leave Him alone so that He may destroy them. That's a big offer, so keep an ear out for what Moses says next.
Nothing in the text has Moses lifting them up, friend. He says he took the two tablets and threw them out of his hands, shattering them before the people's eyes.

Right, baker. Moses says, “…I was afraid of the anger and wrath that the LORD had directed against you, enough to destroy you.” That's the fear he names, and it's about what might happen to the people. I think that shows where his heart was.
Moses says the opposite, baker. He says, “But the LORD listened to me this time as well.” That “as well” tells us the LORD had listened to him before too. So there's no refusal here.

That's right, baker. Moses says, “But the LORD listened to me this time as well.” That “as well” tells us the LORD had listened to him before too. Moses fell down before the LORD, and the LORD heard him.

True, baker. Moses says, “The LORD was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, but at that time I also prayed for Aaron.” Aaron was Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). Praying for him when things were that serious is a good brother move.

It's right there in the text, friend. Moses says, “The LORD was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, but at that time I also prayed for Aaron.” Aaron was his brother (Exodus 4:14), and Moses prayed for him.

Hearing isn't the word Moses uses, friend. The LORD said, “Go up and possess the land that I have given you.” Moses says they rebelled against the command, and that they neither believed Him nor obeyed Him.

Right, baker. Moses prays, “Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Then he asks the LORD to overlook the stubbornness of the people and the wickedness of their sin. He puts those three names right in front of the LORD.

Moses says something different, baker. He went back down the mountain and “…placed the tablets in the ark I had made, as the LORD had commanded me; and there they have remained.” The text puts the tablets in the ark.

That's right, baker. Moses says, “…I went back down the mountain and placed the tablets in the ark I had made, as the LORD had commanded me; and there they have remained.” The text puts the tablets in the ark, not in a tent.

Horeb doesn't come up in this instruction, friend. The LORD tells Moses to continue his journey ahead of the people so they may enter and possess the land He swore to their fathers. That points toward the land.
